page: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock frequency of up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 operations, and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and AES-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 384 GB of RAM, equating to an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A central feature of the hardware configuration is the integrated 11,519 GB local NVMe SSD storage array, which supports high I/O throughput directly attached to the host. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on the host CPU for compute tasks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in data-centric operations. In PassMark tests, the CPU achieved an overall score of 63,100.84, with Geekbench recording a single-core score of 2,161.0 and a multi-core score of 20,273.0. Memory bandwidth reached 223.94 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 95.18 GB/sec for uncached writes. Evaluated database operations and caching scenarios proved high-performing, registering 67.33 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations alongside 82.2 GB/sec static web throughput.

The qualitative profile of the L48s_v4 offers balanced compute density paired with substantial local fast storage and large memory allocations, eliminating external storage latency for temporary or scratch datasets. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled discrete GPUs and the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage. The instance fits heavy relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and a 260 MB L3 cache with Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector support. The system integrates 384 GB of system memory and 11,519 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Synthetic and application benchmarks show strong multi-core and memory performance, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,273.0, uncached memory read bandwidth of 223.94 GB/sec, and 67.33 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides an efficient balance of high-capacity fast scratch storage and substantial RAM, making it tailored for I/O-intensive workloads including high-transaction relational databases, distributed caching layers, big data analytics engines, and large software build systems.
